haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts it. It extracts orders with updated_at after W minus 2 h, up to the replica clock at snapshot start.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open up to 90 min and stamp updated_at at write time, so rows can appear on the replica up to 90 min later.
haiku-low.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at. The next night extracts the changed row again, and the MERGE replaces the older version in fact_orders.
haiku-low.q4: The app soft-deletes by setting deleted_at. The next extract carries is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates that row. Nothing is removed from fact_orders.
haiku-low.q5: Nothing from that attempt commits. The run row is marked failed, the attempt waits 15 min and retries, up to three attempts. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel.
haiku-low.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation finds the mismatch on the order's creation day and reloads that day into the warehouse.
haiku-low.q8: The conditional MERGE on order_id inserts when there is no match, updates only if the staged updated_at is newer, and skips otherwise. So each order_id keeps one row.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in the etl_watermark row as W, the extract upper bound of the last successful attempt. It is written in step 5, in the same transaction as the MERGE, on commit.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 is one warehouse transaction. The MERGE and the W update commit together, so dashboards see all of tonight's changes or none of them.
haiku-low.q11: The failed attempt's staged data is discarded: the next attempt truncates stg_orders, reads the same W, takes a fresh upper bound and re-extracts.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every order created on a mismatched day and applies them via the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. It does not move W.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders with updated_at after W minus 2 h, up to upper (replica clock at snapshot start), within one read snapshot.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open for up to 90 min and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit, so the row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at, so the next night's extract picks the changed row up again and the MERGE updates fact_orders because the staged updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: Deletes are soft (app sets deleted_at, which is also a write). The next night extracts the row with is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates the existing row. No row is removed from fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: Nothing is committed to fact_orders or W. The etl_runs row is marked failed. If fewer than 3 attempts have been made tonight, it waits 15 min and retries. After the third failure it pages on-call.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel (if there is no succeeded etl_runs row for tonight). On-call is separately paged only after the third failed attempt.
sonnet.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation. It finds the mismatch on the order's creation day (within the last 30 days) and re-extracts and reloads every order created that day.
sonnet.q8: The MERGE on order_id is conditional. It updates only if the staged updated_at is newer. If the staged copy is not newer, it skips the row.
sonnet.q9: In the etl_watermark table (one row) in the warehouse. W is set to the attempt's upper bound (replica clock at snapshot start) inside the Step 5 transaction, committed together with the MERGE and the etl_runs succeeded update.
sonnet.q10: Step 5 is a single warehouse transaction, so the MERGE, W update and run status commit together. Dashboards read only fact_orders and so see all of tonight's changes or none.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt truncates stg_orders at its start, so the staged data is discarded. It reads the same W, uses lower = W minus 2 h, takes a fresh upper bound (replica clock at the new snapshot start) and re-extracts.
sonnet.q12: It truncates stg_orders, then re-extracts every order created on a mismatched day. It applies them with the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. W is not changed.
